checks: Source 0354c832e0d018af §§4–5 (9)–(15) has the same strict nonheavy and raw-depth hypotheses. Any two whole fiber masses sum to more than M/2, so two captured centroids would already exceed Q.
Balance covers the middle continuous plane and makes I_0 nonempty. The middle centroid estimate leaves less than γ_d min(a,b) for both endpoints combined, so each endpoint deficit in I_0 is positive.

For a cap below the centroid mass, the signed functional deficit has the right sign. Fubini in the coordinate u·x includes the factor 1/||u||, and the whole parallel slab bounds the mass shortfall even for a supporting or empty trace.

The two endpoint margins sum to twice u_i·(m−y). Subtracting the nonnegative middle margin yields the stated negative-slope bound. Summing the three margins with the same weights cancels the continuous pieces and gives drifts −Δ,0,Δ.
The positive-part lower bounds use the full negative-magnitude sums and retain the signs of ±Δ. The paired sum cancels Δ, and the zero weighted sum of slopes gives the last compensation bound.
